key_insight: MAPS uses a centralized compact latent “proto-plan” to coordinate decentralized vehicle control, separating global strategy from local execution for unsignalized intersections.
engineering_relevance: This architecture offers a practical MARL design pattern for autonomous driving systems that need scalable coordination, lower action-space complexity, and better transfer to larger agent counts.
method: Master agent produces a continuous proto-plan encoding the global coordination strategy.
Worker agents combine the proto-plan with local observations to drive each vehicle independently.
Hierarchical DRL decouples strategic planning from tactical control for modular optimization.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 72 HighwayEnv intersection configurations, MAPS achieved collision-free navigation, reduced average travel time, and reached 94% zero-shot success when trained with three agents and deployed to five-agent scenarios.
watch_item: Results are shown in simulation, so real-world deployment may face sim-to-real gaps and sensitivity to intersection geometry, traffic variability, and coordination timing.
paper_title: Compact Latent Coordination for Autonomous Vehicles at Unsignalized Intersections
